A without the lock (the pick): READY AFTER SMALL FIXES. The build is clean and reproduces: 0 overlaps at zero tolerance with no exemptions, the BOM rebuilt identical, weights confirmed, and the OPEN items written. About a dozen small fixes remain before a shop can build it: the tray's joint and three PEM edge distances; the driver's stud pattern (77.4 x 33.3 against ERP's 77 x 33); a saddle that grips nothing under Ø6; NOTES' cord-cut step; a lead bushing that is not a real part; the driver's model field; five callout-to-CAD mismatches; stale ring, collar, plate and set-screw texts; and RERENDER.md, which misses the cluster's exposed cord and cable ends.
A with the lock: NOT READY. It needs the same fixes, plus its BOM sizes (still from the turned solids) and its datum line (contradicts its 105/285 cables), plus the held lock items.
Today's top and B: NOT READY as packaged. Their NOTES 2 tells the user to pull a lock knob they do not have and says the shade is then locked. That is a one-line fix (branch on the top, not LOCK_ON), then the same small fixes.

missed: BLOCKING, not reported. NOTES 3's cord step cannot be done in place, and the reviewer's status lines say the opposite ('strain relief with ordinary tools (a screwdriver)'; 'v9 cord-cannot-be-wired-as-drawn: FIXED'). The saddle's two M3 pan screws have their heads at x 0.2 to 2.0, at y -+8, z 11 (crystal.py:968). They face the tray's inner wall at x -8 to -7, z 7.4 to 48.4 (crystal.py:913). On my build of A without the lock, a Ø5 screwdriver on either screw's axis runs 7 mm clear, then cuts tray-u, the driver, the tray wall and the canopy (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b110/skeptic-texts-and-build/out/measure-A-nolock.json, from py/measure.py). Approaching from below, past the tray's bottom corner, the driver would have to be more than 30 deg off the screw's axis. The two WAGO 221-412s' lever faces at x -6.7 (crystal.py:974) are 0.3 from the same wall over their full height (z 28.5 to 46.8; measured 0.300). So no lever can be lifted to take the cord's conductors, and no connector can be pulled out toward -x. The plate and tray go up first and the cord's length is set after hanging (NOTES 3). The only way in would be to unbolt the tray and let it hang on its mains leads, and nothing says that. So the cord cannot be clamped or connected as written. The canopy parts are the same in all four tops.

BLOCKING, left UNVERIFIED by the reviewer. The WAGO 221-500 carrier named in the splice row (components.json:1052) and in the NOTES is 17.5 wide, 77.6 high and 25.5 deep from the rail, and weighs 9.8 g (WAGO data sheet 221-500/000-053, https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/4592286.pdf; https://www.wago.com/global/p/221-500). The CAD draws it as a 28 x 18.3 x 1.5 plate (crystal.py:974). In no orientation does it fit the 10 mm between the channel's web (x 3) and the tray's inner wall (x -7), and its 77.6 is longer than the canopy's 45.4 inside height. WAGO's own installation photos show several 221s side by side in one carrier with their levers up, so two connectors in one carrier is plausible. Even so, the splices' 'fixed place', which the T1 Class 2 separation argument (UL 1598 6.17.2) relies on, cannot be built as named and placed. The rivet holes called on the channel (crystal.py:1203-1206) are invented for a part that is not drawn.

Should-fix, text. NOTES 3 never says to cut the suspension cables after leveling, or how much to leave. The CAD draws each cable's tail as 50, 'coiled in the bracket' (crystal.py:731), and the plate closes over the grippers. The suspension row gives no cable length (components.json:722-729). A long supplied 1/16 in stainless cable has nowhere to go, so the installer needs the cut length (about 50 above the gripper, leaving enough to re-level) and the tool (cable cutters).

On the verdict: 'A without the lock: READY AFTER SMALL FIXES' does not hold. The cord cannot be clamped or spliced in place, the named splice carrier does not fit, the real driver cannot go onto its drawn studs (it lands in the -y joint flange and its PEM nut), and the tray joint cannot be made. All four apply to the pick, and to today's top and B, and they need the canopy's inside re-laid out, not text fixes.
